summary: Track B wave L1: Haiku recovers the canonical headers of the remaining game classes, base classes first

open_questions: l3-000: Commit ordering: HEAD b70ac95e ("Track B wave L3b") already contains my rewrites of Rule, RootRule, Path, EndPath, ForceBlock, Block, MgxBlock, Tile, ListRule and RPElem. It was committed while this task was still writing; I ran no git commands. The working copy differs from HEAD only in Exit.hpp (comment), RoomPool.hpp and RandomGenerator.hpp. ListElem.hpp and BlockSearch.hpp were verified and left unchanged. Only the rnd headers were touched, and no layout request in reports/decomp-reconstruction/trackb-batches/layout-requests-g1a.json targets an rnd class.

l3-000: Corrections to the earlier draft, backed by the pseudocode and vtable order: Rule::GetRootRule and Rule::Impl::GetRootRule are non-const; Rule::Impl::Step and Rule::Impl::GetRootRule are virtual (slots 0x10, 0x14); Rule::NewRule is an instance method, not static; Rule::Impl::Impl and RootRule::Impl::Impl signatures are as the queue names them; RootRule::Impl::Generate returns Tile*; Path::Impl::AddExit(vector&, const Exit*, int); Tile::Spawn(Block&, int, int, float, ListElem&) and Tile::TrySpawn(const Exit*, const Exit*, const Exit*, ListElem&) return Tile*; Tile::SaveAsModuleXML takes an int; ListRule::Find returns ListElem by value; RoomPool::Find(std::string) takes its key by value; ListRule size is 0x2c; RoomPool size is 0x14; RPElem size is 0x18 (RoomPool stride 24) with m_pool, m_id and m_recursive; ForceBlock and Path are 0x90 (allocated 0x90 in NewRule); Tile is 0x90 with m_x, m_y, m_z at +0x84..+0x8c; MgxBlock tail is a file buffer at +0x9c0 and an XML document at +0x9c4; Block records are Exit-shaped (Side) with unit/block size fields; the impl subclasses EndPath::Impl, ForceBlock::Impl and Path::Impl carry their source-rule pointer at +0x44 (Path::Impl also has +0x48).

l3-000: rnd::Direction has no header and no queue row. It is forward-declared in Rule.hpp, Block.hpp, Exit.hpp and Tile.hpp. Its layout is a 16-byte record whose first word is the direction id, held in the rnd::Direction::sDirections table, with a rnd::DIRECTION_OPPOSITES table. Needs an owner decision.

l3-000: Bodies will need globals that are not declared in any header: rnd::Direction::sDirections, rnd::DIRECTION_OPPOSITES, rnd::gDistributions and gAssertLevel (plus the unk_956B* data objects used as default Direction records).

l3-000: rnd::TryIsZero (0x489aa4) is a namespace-level function, not a class member. It is declared at the end of Exit.hpp because its only caller is Exit::LoadFromXml. Move it to a free-function header if one is preferred.

l3-000: Partly recovered fields, named unk_ or with a provisional name: RandomGenerator unk_fc and unk_12c (string members, use not recovered); RandomGenerator unk_144 is a directory prefix (LoadBlocks lists <dir>/mgx/mgxlist.txt); Rule unk_80 and unk_84 (the two sizes given to RPElem::FillSizes, default 1); Path unk_8c and unk_8d (read by Path::Impl::OneStep and AddExit) and unk_48 (a packed direction word); RPElem unk_0c, unk_10 and unk_14 (-1 until FillSizes); Rule::Impl child-slot capacity (pad_10 is 0x18 bytes, assumed; the Impl ctor writes slot count+4 without a bounds check); tail bytes of ForceBlock (0x8c..0x8f) and Path (0x8e..0x8f); Block::Side tail (0x100 bytes after +0x2c).

l3-000: Original 32-bit sizes for Exit (0x2c) come from the constructor's writes; no allocation site for it appears in the rnd dumps. Other sizes are from the operator new calls in NewRule, Tile::NewRoot/Spawn, LoadListRules, LoadRoomPools and FromFilename, or from the last field the constructors write.

l3-000: The original std::string is 24 bytes (16 bytes of storage, then the data pointer at +0x14 and the finish pointer at +0x10) and std::vector is 12 bytes, both per the pseudocode. Headers use host types with the 32-bit offsets in the comments, per the layout rules. No static_assert on sizes.

l3-001: Namespaces, not classes: sfc and sfc::script::lua have no layout, so no header was written for either. The owner 'sfc' queue rows are sfc::math::graph templates; their headers already exist under dh2/sfc/math/graph/ (AlgoAStar.hpp is present now, not written by me).

l3-001: LuaScript.hpp still holds Instance and Binder as opaque uint8_t m_instance[12] and m_binder[12] (its comment says the headers are absent). Both are 12 bytes, so the owner can switch to typed members at +0x04 (Instance) and +0x10 (Binder). LuaScript.hpp also says Call(name, args, ret) returns pCall's result, but Instance::pCall is void in the binary (it tail-calls lua_settop), so that claim should be checked.

l3-001: Binder::bindMethod<T> (0x386c20, used by TestUD::createBindings at 0x386d00) is declared only. Its body must split the member pointer into two words and call _bindMethod. The TestUD ledger row is waiting on Binder.hpp.
l3-001: Binder has no constructor in the queue (inlined in the original), so the header declares none. Its owner must set m_instance and m_state. bindMethod does nothing while m_state is zero.

l3-001: Free functions in sfc::script::lua are not declared here: newstate() (0x31b224, internal linkage, called by Instance()) and panic() (0x31a9e8). Arguments(lua_State*, int) is the only ctor that takes a count, so its semantics are documented in the header (count > 0 reads upvalues, count <= 0 reads the stack after skipping -count values).

l3-001: Return types were taken from the assembly, not the decompile. pCall (all overloads), pCall_, execFile, setError, setGlobal, registerFunction, bindMethod and _bindMethod are void because they end in tail calls to void Lua API functions. loadFile(StreamBuffer&) and loadFile(IFileStream&) return Error by value: the first is confirmed in asm (R0 is the sret pointer, R1 is this, R2 is the stream), and the second matches the decompile.

l3-001: Evidence-based names that are not string, binding or save-field names: Instance::m_ownsState (+0x08), Arguments::m_values (+0x04), Error::m_status (+0x04), Binder::m_instance (+0x04) and m_state (+0x08). Rename or switch to unk_ names if the integrator prefers the strict rule.

l3-001: Error: the message string is a 24-byte STLport string at +0x08 (inferred from the original 0x20 span, which ReturnValues.hpp uses for its embedded Error). Arguments::operator[] returns const Value& where the binary returns a pointer to the element, which has the same ABI. _chunkReader takes size_t* where the binary uses unsigned int*.

l3-001: Sibling headers Value.hpp and ReturnValues.hpp (written by another agent) were checked: a TU that includes all six headers compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra. ReturnValues.hpp still reserves Error as pad_04[0x20] and can now embed sfc::script::lua::Error directly. LuaManager::AddFile (ledger 0x37b23c, partial) was waiting on Instance.hpp and Error.hpp, which now exist.

l3-002: Category mismatch: sfc::script::lua::Value and ReturnValues are listed under category game-app, but their queue rows (game-app/queue.csv) carry owner lib-lua. Headers were written at the paths the task specifies (dh2/sfc/script/lua/<Class>.hpp).

l3-002: unsigned char StreamReader and unsigned int StreamReader are not classes. They are template specializations of StreamReader::readAs/writeAs (0x3365a4, 0x336718, 0x3139e0, 0x3df1a0 and related). Their owner is port/decomp-reconstruction/game/include/dh2/StreamReader.hpp, which already exists and declares readAs<unsigned char>(IStreamBase*) and writeAs<unsigned char>. No header was created: 'unsigned char StreamReader.hpp' is not a valid class header name. StreamReader.hpp is outside this assignment and was not edited. Its comment lists readAs<unsigned short>(IStreamBase*, unsigned short*) at 0x5075b8, but no explicit specialization is declared for it; the StreamReader owner should add that declaration.

l3-002: ReturnValues +0x04: the ctor (0x31b434) constructs sfc::script::lua::Error at this+4 and the dtor destroys it. No Error header exists (Error ctors and dtors are in lib-lua queue at 0x31a68c..0x31a980). The 0x20-byte pad_04 is a gap-fill sized to the next known field at +0x24, not a measured Error size. When an Error header lands, replace pad_04 with the member.

l3-002: ReturnValues original object size is not in class-facts and no allocation size was found. The header records only the fields the ctor and methods touch (vptr, Error at +0x04, list pointer at +0x24).

l3-002: Value +0x0c..+0x23 and +0x24..+0x6f: the narrow and wide string storage is an STLport-style layout. Fields at +0x0c (end or inline buffer), +0x1c (end), +0x20 (data) are confirmed by getString, _pushOnStack, the copy ctor and the dtor. The wide string is touched only by the copy ctor, operator= and the dtor. Its bytes from +0x2c to +0x63 are unrecovered (pad_24[0x40]).

l3-002: Return types of Value::_setFromStack and ReturnValues::_addFromStack are declared int. Hex-Rays types them float because lua_type's result is pun-stored into the tag. Confidence is low; verify against assembly if it matters.

l3-002: Value setters (setNil, setBool, setNumber, setPointer, setUserData, setString) are declared void. Hex-Rays returns this/the string object from them, which looks like compiler leftover rather than source.

l3-003: Class list: the task text said only "batch". That is the group id l3-003 (classes ["batch"]) in reports/decomp-reconstruction/trackb-batches/l3-groups.json, and l1-063 in l1-groups.json also lists "batch" among four real classes. The queue owner "batch" is the namespace batch::, so I took it to mean batch::BatchNodeCompiler (with nested SGameObjectLinkedCallback) and batch::GOBatchSceneNode. Both headers already existed and were completed in place. The group files should list these two classes.

l3-003: BatchNodeCompiler has no constructor symbol. Level::_LoadBatchInit (0x3f240c) does operator new(56) and writes the fields inline (m_compiled, list and map empty, callback vptr, m_batchNode null). No constructor is declared because none is queued. game-world/src/g1-game-world-Level-7c7f5d-2.cpp uses new batch::BatchNodeCompiler(), which value-initializes and does not set the callback vptr or map header the way the original does. The integrator needs to decide whether to declare an inline constructor.

l3-003: GOBatchSceneNode has no constructor symbol. Compile (0x50dc84) builds it inline after operator new(360) and calls glitch::scene::CBatchSceneNode::CBatchSceneNode() with no arguments in the Hex-Rays output. The canonical glitch-scene-collada-gui/scene/CBatchSceneNode.hpp declares only id-taking constructors. The register arguments of that call need a check in the assembly before Compile can be written against the canonical base.

l3-003: Vtable offsets: the comments use the offsets decomp_vtable.py prints (callback slots 0x00/0x04/0x08, GOBatchSceneNode dtor slots 0x14/0x18 and isSegmentVisible 0x114). The offset base is not confirmed. The GOBatchSceneNode dtor at 0x50dabc stores the primary vptr as symbol + 0x1c, but Compile calls vptr + 0x48, which matches the tool's +0x54 setVisible only if the vptr is symbol + 0x0c. Those two readings disagree, so check the address-point convention before relying on the numeric slot comments.

l3-003: Layout request for GameObject (owner dh2/GameObject.hpp): GameObject +0x80 (uint8_t) is a visibility gate read by batch::GOBatchSceneNode::isSegmentVisible (0x50cd44). GameObject +0x2ee and +0x2f0 (uint8_t) are read there too. A virtual at GameObject vtable +0xc4 is called there. The callback batch::BatchNodeCompiler::SGameObjectLinkedCallback::operator() (0x3efe58) writes GameObject +0x2fc (uint8_t) = 1 as the visible byte.

l3-003: No layout was added for GOBatchSceneNode beyond the base. The class has no members of its own: the object is 0x168 bytes, and the +0x160 vptr and +0x164 count are the glitch::IReferenceCounted virtual base already declared through ISceneNode and the canonical CBatchSceneNode. The previous unk_160 / unk_164 members duplicated that base and were removed. Nothing else in the tree reads them. The second glitch::io::IAttributeExchangingObject construction vtable named in the dtor is at offset 0 in the primary chain, not a second base.
